content: The certification course for pest control operators should cover the following topics in detail: 1. Pesticide Laws and Regulations: A comprehensive understanding of the country's pesticide laws and regulations is essential. 2. General Information on Pesticides: This includes the importance of pesticides, their formulations, selecting appropriate chemical control strategies, and ensuring the safe handling and use of pesticides. 3. Pesticide Poisoning: Recognition of symptoms of pesticide poisoning, along with first aid and decontamination procedures, should be emphasized. 4. Integrated Pest or Vector Management: Training should include strategies for integrated pest or vector management. 5. Biology and Ecology of Major Pests: This involves understanding the biology, ecology, public health, and economic significance of major pests, as well as their identification. 6. Pesticide Application Equipment: 7. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Proper use and importance of personal protective equipment must be covered. 8. Re-entry Intervals: Knowledge of re-entry intervals after pesticide application is critical. 9. Safety Data Sheets: Training on how to read and use Safety Data Sheets (SDS) is necessary. 10. Operational Procedures: This includes preparation of spray materials, precautions, and ensuring quality and effective pesticide applications. 11. Proper Handling of Pesticides: Safe handling practices, including the disposal of unwanted pesticides and containers, as well as spill prevention and management, should be addressed. 12. Management of Public Health Pests: This includes the management of vectors, pests of public health importance, stored product pests, and structural pests like termites, with a focus on their life cycles, susceptible stages, and habitat identification. 13. Record-Keeping: Operators should be trained in maintaining accurate records of their operations. 14. Familiarity with Guidelines: Operators must be familiar with the Code of Conduct, technical guidelines, and national guidelines related to pest control operations. 15. Special Training for Fumigation: Those intending to perform fumigation activities must undergo specialized training and examination on fumigation techniques. For assistant pest control operator certification, the syllabus should include: 1. General information on pesticides, including formulations, selecting appropriate chemical control strategies, and safe handling and use. 2. Proper use of pesticide application equipment in the public health sector. 3. Operational procedures, preparation of spray materials, precautions, and ensuring quality and effective pesticide applications. 4. Biology and ecology of major pests, their public health and economic importance, and their identification. 5. Proper use of personal protective equipment. 6. Knowledge of re-entry intervals after pesticide application. 7. Training on reading and using Safety Data Sheets. 8. Proper handling of pesticides, including disposal of unwanted pesticides and containers. 9. Record-keeping of operations. 10. Familiarity with national guidelines on pest control operations and accessing them. For fumigation certification (Category B), the syllabus should include: 1. Types of fumigation, such as space fumigation and soil fumigation. 2. 3. Advantages and disadvantages of fumigation. 4. Factors affecting the effectiveness of fumigation. Additional topics may be included in the syllabus based on local requirements and situations.
